hook: A principal wants 100 students’ opinions on a new schedule. She could number all 1,200 students and pick 100 by chance, pick 25 from each grade, pick four whole homerooms, or take every 12th name on a list. All four are random. They differ in cost, in convenience, and in how well they guarantee that every grade is heard.

prereq.q: A school wants to know what its 1,200 students think. What is the population?
prereq.why: The population is the whole group the question is about.

prereq.q: A study asks 100 students their opinion without imposing anything. What kind of study is it?
prereq.why: It asks a sample questions, so it is a sample survey, an observational study.

figure.caption: One population of 48 students, four random samples: simple random, stratified by grade, cluster (two whole homerooms) and systematic (every 6th after a random start).

chain.cause: Use chance, not judgment, to choose the sample
chain.effect: no one’s preferences decide who is in it, so it tends to represent the population

chain.cause: Label every individual in the sampling frame and pick labels at random, skipping repeats
chain.effect: you get a simple random sample: every group of n has the same chance

chain.cause: Split the population into strata of similar individuals and sample each
chain.effect: every group is represented, and estimates vary less when strata differ

chain.cause: Choose whole clusters, or every kth individual after a random start
chain.effect: sampling is cheaper and easier, at some cost in precision or with a risk from patterns in the list

ideas: A simple random sample (SRS) of size n gives every group of n individuals the same chance of being chosen. Procedure: label, generate random numbers, skip repeats, select.
Sampling without replacement means each individual can be chosen once; with replacement allows repeats.
A stratified random sample splits the population into strata of similar individuals and takes an SRS from each.
A cluster sample chooses whole groups at random and measures everyone in them. A systematic random sample takes every kth individual after a random start.
The sampling frame is the list the sample is drawn from.

misconception.wrong: "Use a random number generator to choose 10 ponds" is a complete procedure.
misconception.right: Someone else could not follow it. Say how the ponds are labeled (1 to 80), what is generated (whole numbers from 1 to 80), what to do with repeats (skip them) and when to stop (10 different ponds).

summary: Random sampling uses chance to choose individuals from a sampling frame. A simple random sample gives every group of n the same chance; a stratified sample takes an SRS within each stratum of similar individuals; a cluster sample takes whole groups chosen at random; a systematic sample takes every kth individual after a random start. Write procedures as label, generate, skip repeats, select.
